blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: This tree follows the topics and the problem list of NeetCode's roadmap (the NeetCode 150), with a learning page written for this site for each topic. The explanations and Java templates are ours; the problems belong to LeetCode, and each one links to its LeetCode page.

A **trie** (prefix tree) stores strings one character per edge. All words that share a prefix share the path from the root. That makes **prefix questions** cost O(length of the prefix), no matter how many words are stored: "does any word start with `pre`?", "list all words with this prefix", "does this string match a pattern with wildcards?".

A `HashSet<String>` answers "is this exact word present?" just as fast, but it cannot answer prefix questions without scanning every word. That contrast is the whole case for a trie.

| Operation | Trie | `HashSet<String>` |
|---|---|---|
| Insert / exact search a word of length L | O(L) | O(L) to hash |
| Does any word start with prefix p? | O(len p) | O(n · L), scan all |
| Enumerate all words with a prefix | O(len p + output) | O(n · L) |
| Memory | Up to 26 pointers per node | Strings only |
"prefix", "autocomplete", "dictionary of words", "word search in a grid with many words", "wildcard '.'", "longest common prefix".
blocks.title: Signal words

blocks.text: A node holds an array of children (26 for lowercase letters) and a flag marking the end of a word. Use a `HashMap<Character, Node>` instead when the alphabet is large or unknown.

blocks.title: TrieTemplates.java

blocks.text:
**What to notice.** `search` and `startsWith` share `find`; the only difference is the final `word` check, which is also the most common bug: forgetting it makes `search("app")` succeed when only `"apple"` was inserted.

### Word Search II: a trie plus backtracking

Searching a grid for many words one at a time repeats work. Build a trie of all the words, then run one DFS from every cell, walking the trie in step with the grid: stop a path the moment the current letters are not a prefix of any word. Store the complete word at its end node, mark visited cells in place while exploring, and **remove found words and empty branches** from the trie to prune future searches. That pruning is what makes the hard version pass.

- **Forgetting the end-of-word flag**, so prefixes count as words.
- **Memory.** `Node[26]` per node is large when words are few and long. A `HashMap` or a compressed (radix) trie is smaller.
- **Alphabet assumptions.** `c - 'a'` throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` on uppercase letters or digits.
- **Recursion depth** equals word length, which is fine, but wildcard search can branch 26 ways per level.

When queries depend on prefixes: autocomplete, "is there any word starting with ...", or pruning a search early as in Word Search II. For plain membership tests a hash set is simpler and uses less memory.
blocks.title: Interview angle: When would you choose a trie over a hash set?
Key points
blocks.text:
- A trie shares prefixes, so prefix queries cost O(length of the prefix)
- Each node needs children plus an end-of-word flag
- `search` is `find` plus a check of the flag; `startsWith` is just `find`
- Wildcards turn a search into DFS over children
- Word Search II = trie plus grid DFS, pruning as words are found
- Use a map for children when the alphabet is not tiny

The NeetCode 150 problems for **Tries**: 3 in all (0 easy, 2 medium, 1 hard), in the order NeetCode lists them. Do the easy ones first, then the medium ones. For every problem, write down the idea and the complexity in one sentence before you look at a solution.

items.question: Why does a trie answer "does any word start with this prefix?" faster than a hash set?
items.answer: Following the prefix's characters down the trie takes O(length of the prefix) and the existence of the path is the answer. A hash set has no way to ask about prefixes, so it would scan every stored word.

items.question: What goes wrong if `search` only checks that the path exists?
items.answer: It returns true for any prefix of a stored word, for example `search("app")` after inserting only "apple". You must also check that a word ends at the final node.

items.question: How does a trie speed up Word Search II compared with running Word Search for each word?
items.answer: One DFS explores the grid once for all words together, and a path is abandoned as soon as its letters are not a prefix of any word in the trie. Searching per word repeats the grid exploration for every word.
